tagline: Real-world execution benchmarks for bioinformatics AI agents

benchmarks.name: cross_domain_routing
benchmarks.task: Given a natural-language analysis request, name the single correct WORKFLOW that should run it (targets are public nf-core pipeline names where applicable). Credit for acceptable_alts.

benchmarks.name: param_prefill
benchmarks.task: Extract structured parameters from a natural-language request; do not fill parameters that were not specified (must_not_fill).

benchmarks.name: protocol_thresholds
benchmarks.task: Given a sequencing protocol and a generic QC threshold, decide whether the sample is biologically VALID and whether it should PASS or FAIL — vs the naive universal-threshold action.

benchmarks.name: autofix_benchmark
benchmarks.task: Given a failed pipeline run and its error log, classify the failure into one of 10 objective fix categories (genome_mismatch, resource_failure, container_error, dependency_mismatch, missing_input, param_type_error, param_scope_error, data_format_error, output_assertion_error, cloud_storage_error). A free-text 'expected_fix' reference is provided as a secondary signal.

benchmarks.name: workflow_generation
benchmarks.task: Given a research intent, select the correct analysis category (partition A) OR identify the required key tools (partition B). Both ground truths are standard and catalog-neutral.

benchmarks.name: boin_benchmark
benchmarks.task: Given a BOIN dose-escalation scenario, produce the correct dose decision.

benchmarks.name: pbpk_benchmark
benchmarks.task: Given a compound (SMILES), dose and route, predict PK; reference = published clinical PK values.

benchmarks.name: drug_discovery_e2e
benchmarks.task: Given a protein structure (PDB) and ligands with experimental Kd, reproduce the affinity rank order.

benchmarks.name: proteomics_search
benchmarks.task: RUN (not predict) a shotgun-proteomics MS/MS search against a human proteome + entrapment DB and report speed (wall-clock, spectra/s) AND recall (#PSMs/#peptides/#proteins at 1% FDR) on the same runs, with the 1% FDR validated by entrapment false-match-rate. Scored by running the committed Nextflow harness, not by a predictions.jsonl. Targets: >=5x faster end-to-end than the brute-force (Comet) baseline; no peptide-recall regression; entrapment FMR <=1.3% at claimed 1% FDR. See proteomics_search/metadata.json + README.md.

note: Public neutralized export for fair cross-system comparison. Internal source not included.
